replication.target_description: Experiment 3: seated/standing within-participant attention task. Source located, but supplied description does not uniquely identify an outcome and ANOVA term. See candidate evidence in notes.

n.sample_role: Participants; common experiment-level analytic N retained only as a candidate pending row correspondence.
n.exclusions: 50 recruited; all met inclusion criteria; no participants excluded for losing more than 20% of data. No premature RT trials; 3.15% error/time-out trials excluded from RT; 1.34% remaining correct RT trials trimmed.

reported_success.quote: Smith et al.’s Experiment 3. While we found an effect of ... posture on set size in the PE data, this effect seems rather ... spurious and less robust than what Smith et al. initially ... reported. Moreover, we failed to find an effect of posture ... on set size in the RT analyses.

notes: Primary-source identity verified from full research article: The Influence of Posture on Attention, Emilie E. Caron and nine coauthors matching the reference (full text gives Reynolds J. Ballotti), DOI 10.1027/1618-3169/a000567, Experimental Psychology (2022), 69(6), 295–307; online publication February 21, 2023. Includes methods, results, discussion, references and appendix. Not an abstract or preregistration. No PDF supplied. Every assigned unfinished field examined. Original/unassigned fields are placeholders. Target ambiguity remains across ANOVA terms and/or RT versus PE; no row-order or numeric matching used. Explicit analyzed participant N candidate = 50; not derived from df, recruitment total, or group sum. Primary RT: posture ηp2 = .118, p = .014, F(1,49) = 6.54; set size ηp2 = .884, p < .001, F(1,49) = 373.76; posture × set size ηp2 < .001, p = .861, F(1,49) = 0.03. Primary PE: set size ηp2 = .274, p < .001; posture ηp2 = .015, p = .388; interaction ηp2 = .086, p = .037, F(1,49) = 4.61. Appendix conventional PE interaction ηp2 = .013, p = .434. Article names the RT interaction its main Experiment 3 target, but the supplied row permits multiple terms/outcomes. Mixed records the authors’ RT failure and PE finding they call spurious; pp. 303–304 attribute the PE finding entirely to treating slow responses as errors and refrain from interpreting it as meaningful. All candidates are printed partial eta-squared; each p shown belongs to its associated test. No conversion or coefficient selected. Reported success is an author narrative at experiment level, independently of unresolved coefficient correspondence.
